Maya: quick idea  what about 'tentative commits' instead of short soft leases? primary writes create a tentative record (id) visible locally; remote regions accept tentatives but final commit is deterministic (majority or timeout). aim: avoid sync cross-region commits while letting global tenants continue.

Ravi: sounds like optimistic multi-master. main worry is who finalizes commit. if we avoid control-plane decisions, we need a deterministic rule in the data-plane so proxies can proceed without extra round trips.

Tom: header sketch i'm prototyping:
X-Residency-Mode: TENTATIVE
X-Tentative-ID: tnt-20250615-778
X-Commit-After-Ack: 2

Maya: read/caching behavior: local cache may serve tentative values tagged with `cache-tentative=true`. clients can opt into `visibility=committed` to avoid tentatives. responses include `X-Visibility: committed|tentative`.

policy-bot: policy alert: tenant=brightco-eu residue=HARD_LOCAL -> block tentative write outbound (policy p-2025-07).

Ravi: conflict resolution: prefer app-level merge when available; otherwise LWW with tombstone versioning. reconcilers must surface conflicts to metrics so product can follow up.

Tom: operational controls: tentative TTL (default 2m), bounded backlog queue; when queue full emit `X-Tentative-Backpressure: true`. also provide `tentative-abort` endpoint for emergency cleanup.

Maya: metrics to add: tentative-created-rate, commit-latency.p50/p95, tentative-conflict-rate, tentative-abort-rate-by-tenant. alarms if abort-rate spikes for HARD_LOCAL tenants.

Ravi: runbook note: manual force-commit / abort steps; how to quarantine tenant; how to fast-forward reconciler. i'll draft.

Tom: perf note: bundle tentatives into batched protobuf envelopes on the wire to reduce per-key overhead. data-plane should own token grafting and commit decision.

Maya: canary plan: enable TENTATIVE for GLOBAL tenants at 1% traffic in us-west-2 next week. ops-bot, schedule?

ops-bot: scheduled: tentative-commit canary -> 2025-06-18T14:00:00Z (1% GLOBAL, us-west-2). notifications to #infra-metrics.

Maya: follow-ups: Tom opens proxy PR for headers + cache tags, Ravi drafts runbook and policy checks, I'll implement tentative reconciler and metrics. will report canary results back here. :)
